label: Industrial Revolution
description: Mechanization, factories, urbanization, new class relations, technological acceleration, and modern mass society.

label: Kalevala
description: Elias Lönnrot’s compilation of runo-song materials; a major source for later national and fantasy mythmaking.

label: Goethe — Faust
description: Scholar bargains with Mephistopheles; knowledge, striving, desire, modernity, and damnation/redemption.

label: Mary Shelley — Frankenstein
description: Gothic-scientific novel about creation, responsibility, alienation, ambition, and social rejection.

label: Mary Shelley — The Last Man
description: Early modern apocalyptic novel imagining a plague-driven end of humanity.

label: Edgar Allan Poe
description: Poet and fiction writer central to Gothic horror, the detective story, ratiocination, and theories of literary effect.

label: Melville — Moby-Dick
description: Whaling epic mixing adventure, scripture, Shakespearean drama, natural history, obsession, and metaphysics.

label: Browning — Childe Roland to the Dark Tower Came
description: Oblique dramatic monologue of a doomed quest through a blasted landscape toward the Dark Tower.

label: Whitman — Leaves of Grass
description: Expansive poetic project on body, democracy, selfhood, nation, labor, sexuality, and voice.

label: Tolstoy — War and Peace
description: Historical novel on war, family, contingency, history, and ordinary life against grand theories.

label: Fyodor Dostoevsky
description: Novelist of moral psychology, belief, freedom, guilt, extremity, ideology, and polyphonic conflict.

label: The Brothers Karamazov
description: Family and philosophical novel on faith, freedom, guilt, patricide, responsibility, and suffering.

label: Twain — Adventures of Huckleberry Finn
description: Vernacular journey novel confronting slavery, conscience, friendship, performance, and national mythology.

label: Stevenson — Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde
description: Gothic novella of divided identity, repression, experiment, reputation, and urban modernity.

label: William Morris
description: Designer, socialist, medievalist and fantasy precursor whose romances helped shape secondary-world fantasy.

label: Morris — The Well at the World’s End
description: Quest romance often treated as a precursor of modern secondary-world fantasy.

label: H. G. Wells — The Time Machine
description: Scientific romance using time travel to extrapolate class division and human evolution.

label: H. G. Wells — The War of the Worlds
description: Invasion narrative reversing imperial perspective and confronting technological vulnerability.

label: Owen Wister — The Virginian
description: Landmark 1902 Western set in Wyoming. Wister's cowboy hero helped establish a durable genre formula around personal honor, the 'Code of the West,' frontier law, the tenderfoot observer, a climactic gunfight, and tension between Eastern social norms and Western identity; later Western fiction and film repeatedly reused or revised these conventions.

label: Jack London — The Call of the Wild
description: Adventure/naturalist novel of domestication, violence, environment, and return to wildness.

label: Lord Dunsany
description: Early fantasy writer noted for invented mythologies, dreamlike prose, distant gods, and secondary worlds.

label: Kafka — The Metamorphosis
description: Absurd transformation becomes a lens on family, labor, shame, bureaucracy, and alienation.

label: World War I
description: Industrialized mass war reshaped modernist aesthetics, political imagination, trauma, disillusionment, and mythic reconstruction.

label: Joyce — Ulysses
description: Modernist novel mapping ordinary Dublin life onto Homeric structure while radically experimenting with style.

label: T. S. Eliot — The Waste Land
description: Modernist collage of voices, myths, urban exhaustion, war aftermath, ritual, and cultural fragments.
